I cant see Uber and Lyft going away any time soon and I was hoping they could perhaps fill a short cheap trip hole in the market but I'm really curious to find out how you came to your opinion on it.

Their whole business model rides on a loophole in the system. They are not considered taxis, they are considered "ride sharing" which is why they don't have to get taxi licenses or deal with half of the oversight or liability of being an actual taxi company. Employees are also considered independent contractors which means they're responsible for literally every cost associated with their job including tracking and paying their own taxes, insurance, vehicle maintenance, and dozens of other costs. They have to use their own insurance and claim any damage that occurs on it which sends premiums sky high and many companies will drop you or hike your rates if they find out you're using your car for work.

They lure people in by promising theyll make like 2 grand a week but they don't tell them that they'll have to basically cut that in half once they account for all the real costs of having the job.

And then to top it off your whole job rides on a rating system that is easily abused and can get you fired on the spot. Literally all you have to do to get an Uber driver fired is report smelling weed when you leave your driver review.

Basically, they make milions by skirting the law and abusing several loopholes all while taking advantage of mostly college kids or people who need extra money.
